organs.name: Oral cavity & oropharynx (incl. tongue, tonsils)
organs.covers: Mouth/Oral cavity; Tongue; Tonsils; + odontogenic lesions (jaws)

organs.name: Placenta, umbilical cord, membranes & gestational trophoblastic disease
Paraganglia & neuroendocrine system (extra-adrenal paraganglioma, carotid body)
Central nervous system - brain, meninges & pineal
Ocular adnexa & orbit (eyelid, lacrimal gland, conjunctiva)

entities.variants: Puerperal (lactational) mastitis; non-puerperal mastitis; mastitis neonatorum; peripheral vs subareolar abscess
entities.remarks: Usually Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA increasingly) or Streptococcus via nipple fissures in early lactation; neutrophilic infiltrate, necrosis, abscess formation.

entities.entity: Subareolar abscess / recurrent subareolar abscess (Zuska disease)
entities.variants: Squamous metaplasia of lactiferous ducts (SMOLD); mammary duct (periareolar) fistula
entities.remarks: Keratinising squamous metaplasia of lactiferous ducts → keratin plugging, rupture, keratin granulomas, sinus tract opening at areolar margin; strongly associated with smoking.

entities.variants: Plasma cell mastitis (plasma-cell-rich variant)
entities.remarks: Periductal chronic inflammation ± duct rupture; overlaps with duct ectasia; smoking association; may mimic carcinoma clinically (nipple retraction, mass).
Distinctive suppurative lipogranulomas with central clear (cystic) vacuoles rimmed by neutrophils; Gram-positive bacilli (Corynebacterium spp., esp. C. kroppenstedtii) within vacuoles.
Lobulocentric non-necrotising granulomas with neutrophils/microabscesses; young parous women; diagnosis of exclusion (rule out TB, fungi, Corynebacterium, sarcoid).

entities.variants: Nodular, disseminated, sclerosing; primary vs secondary (spread from chest wall/axillary nodes)
entities.remarks: Caseating epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells; AFB/ZN, CBNAAT/GeneXpert, culture; important differential in India; may mimic carcinoma.

entities.variants: Often post-implant / post-procedure / nipple-piercing related
entities.remarks: Granulomatous inflammation; rapidly growing mycobacteria (M. fortuitum, M. abscessus, M. chelonae); culture/molecular confirmation.

entities.variants: Primary; secondary (from thoracic actinomycosis)
entities.remarks: Sulfur granules with filamentous Gram-positive bacteria, abscesses and sinus tracts.

entities.variants: Syphilis (chancre of nipple, gumma); brucellosis; cat-scratch disease (Bartonella; intramammary node); leprosy
entities.remarks: Rare; mostly case reports; correlate with serology / special stains / molecular tests.

entities.variants: Blastomycosis; histoplasmosis; cryptococcosis; aspergillosis; coccidioidomycosis; candidal mastitis/nipple candidiasis (lactation)
entities.remarks: Granulomatous ± suppurative inflammation; GMS/PAS for organisms; often immunocompromised host (except lactational Candida).

entities.variants: Wuchereria bancrofti; Brugia malayi; Dirofilaria (zoonotic)
entities.remarks: Endemic in India; painless mass with eosinophil-rich granulomatous inflammation around degenerating worms; microfilariae may be seen on FNAC; may calcify.

entities.variants: Echinococcus granulosus
entities.remarks: Laminated acellular membrane, germinal layer and protoscolices/hooklets; rare primary site.

entities.variants: Cysticercosis (Taenia solium); sparganosis; trichinosis
entities.remarks: Cysticercus: cyst with scolex, surrounding granulomatous/eosinophilic reaction; endemic in India.

entities.variants: Herpes simplex (lactational nipple HSV); herpes zoster; molluscum contagiosum
entities.remarks: Skin-type lesions; viral cytopathic changes.
Non-necrotising well-formed granulomas; usually with systemic disease; exclude infection and granulomatous lobular mastitis.

entities.variants: Silicone granuloma (siliconoma, from rupture/bleed or injection); paraffinoma; suture granuloma; reaction to other injected fillers (e.g. polyacrylamide gel)
entities.remarks: Vacuolated histiocytes, multinucleated giant cells around refractile/non-birefringent material; silicone may spread to axillary nodes (silicone lymphadenopathy).

entities.variants: Diabetic (type 1 DM) and non-diabetic (autoimmune: Hashimoto, SLE) forms
entities.remarks: Dense keloid-like fibrosis, perilobular/periductal/perivascular B-lymphocytic infiltrate, epithelioid myofibroblasts; hard mass mimicking carcinoma.

entities.variants: Sclerosing mastitis; inflammatory pseudotumour-type
entities.remarks: Lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, storiform fibrosis, obliterative phlebitis; IgG4+ plasma cells >50/HPF and IgG4/IgG ratio >40%.

entities.variants: Lupus panniculitis (profundus) of breast
entities.remarks: Lobular panniculitis with hyaline fat necrosis, lymphoid aggregates/germinal centres, lymphocytic vasculitis; SLE/discoid lupus.

entities.variants: Giant cell arteritis; granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA); polyarteritis nodosa; eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
entities.remarks: May present as a mass; localized or part of systemic vasculitis.

entities.variants: Atopic, contact, irritant dermatitis; psoriasis
entities.remarks: Spongiotic dermatitis; key clinical differential of Paget disease (Paget cells absent; CK7 negative intraepidermal cells).

entities.variants: Synovial metaplasia of capsule; silicone-laden histiocytes; calcified capsule
entities.remarks: Fibrous capsule with synovial-like metaplasia, chronic inflammation; examine effusion/capsule for BIA-ALCL when seroma present.

entities.variants: Amastia (absent breast + nipple); amazia (absent breast tissue, nipple present); athelia (absent nipple); hypoplasia; Poland syndrome association
entities.remarks: Congenital; Poland syndrome = unilateral pectoralis major absence with breast/limb anomalies.

entities.variants: Polymastia (supernumerary breast); polythelia (supernumerary nipple); axillary accessory breast tissue; aberrant breast tissue (vulva, milk-line sites)
entities.remarks: Along embryonic milk line, commonest in axilla; subject to all diseases of normal breast incl. fibroadenoma and carcinoma.

entities.entity: Congenital nipple inversion / tubular (tuberous) breast deformity
entities.remarks: Developmental; acquired nipple inversion should prompt exclusion of carcinoma/duct ectasia.

entities.variants: Juvenile (pubertal) hypertrophy; gestational gigantomastia; drug-induced (D-penicillamine)
entities.remarks: Massive diffuse enlargement; stromal and ductal proliferation without lobule formation, PASH-like stroma common.

entities.variants: Gross cysts (blue-domed cysts); microcysts; apocrine metaplasia; stromal fibrosis; mild (usual) hyperplasia; simple adenosis
entities.remarks: Non-proliferative breast disease; no or minimal increase in cancer risk (RR ~1).

entities.variants: Simple cyst; apocrine cyst; cyst with calcium oxalate (weddellite) crystals; ruptured cyst
entities.remarks: Lined by flattened or apocrine epithelium with myoepithelial layer; calcium oxalate crystals (birefringent) mostly in apocrine cysts.

entities.variants: Simple apocrine metaplasia; papillary apocrine change (simple/complex); atypical apocrine metaplasia
entities.remarks: Eosinophilic granular cytoplasm, apical snouts, AR+/GCDFP-15+, ER/PR−; atypical apocrine change needs comparison with apocrine DCIS (nuclear enlargement ≥3x, necrosis).

entities.entity: Other metaplastic changes of breast epithelium
entities.variants: Squamous metaplasia (in cysts, papillomas, post-biopsy, gynaecomastia); clear cell change/metaplasia; mucinous/goblet cell metaplasia (rare); myoid metaplasia
entities.remarks: Benign; recognise to avoid over-calling carcinoma (e.g. clear cell change vs clear cell DCIS/LCIS).

entities.variants: Mild, moderate, florid; gynaecomastoid hyperplasia; UDH within papilloma/radial scar
entities.remarks: WHO 5th: benign epithelial proliferation; heterogeneous cells, streaming, irregular slit-like secondary lumina; mosaic CK5/6 and ER heterogeneous; not a direct precursor; RR ~1.5–2.

entities.entity: Columnar cell change / columnar cell hyperplasia (without atypia)
entities.variants: Columnar cell change (1–2 layers); columnar cell hyperplasia (>2 layers, may form tufts)
entities.remarks: Enlarged TDLU acini lined by columnar cells with apical snouts, intraluminal secretions ± calcifications; ER strong diffuse; no atypia (cf. flat epithelial atypia).

entities.variants: Simple adenosis; blunt duct adenosis
entities.remarks: Increased number of acini per lobule with preserved two-cell layer.

entities.variants: Nodular sclerosing adenosis ('adenosis tumour'); sclerosing adenosis with apocrine metaplasia; with perineural/vascular 'invasion'; involved by ALH/LCIS/DCIS
entities.remarks: WHO 5th benign sclerosing lesion; lobulocentric, compressed distorted acini with myoepithelial layer (p63, calponin, SMMHC) — key mimic of invasive/tubular carcinoma; RR ~1.5–2.

entities.variants: Sclerosing adenosis with apocrine metaplasia; atypical apocrine adenosis
entities.remarks: WHO 5th entity; apocrine cells in an adenosis lesion; myoepithelium retained; atypical form shows marked nuclear enlargement — distinguish from invasive apocrine carcinoma.

entities.variants: Radial scar (<10 mm); complex sclerosing lesion (≥10 mm); with UDH, ADH, LCIS/DCIS or papilloma
entities.remarks: Central fibroelastotic core with entrapped tubules and radiating proliferative ducts; mimics carcinoma on imaging; myoepithelial markers confirm benignity; excision vs VAE depending on atypia.
Adenosis with prominent myoepithelial hyperplasia; overlaps with/may accompany adenomyoepithelioma.
Young women; multiple cysts with apocrine metaplasia, papillary UDH, duct papillomatosis and sclerosing adenosis; marker of family history of breast cancer.

entities.variants: Cystic hypersecretory change; cystic hypersecretory hyperplasia
entities.remarks: Cystically dilated ducts with colloid-like eosinophilic secretion (thyroid follicle-like) with retraction artefact; spectrum extends to atypical CHH and cystic hypersecretory DCIS.

entities.variants: Without atypia; with ADH; with DCIS
entities.remarks: Mucin-filled cysts with extravasated acellular mucin; must exclude mucinous carcinoma (floating epithelium in mucin without myoepithelium favours carcinoma).

entities.variants: Collagenous spherulosis involving papilloma/sclerosing adenosis; involved by LCIS
entities.remarks: Intraluminal eosinophilic/basement membrane spherules surrounded by myoepithelial cells; incidental; mimic of adenoid cystic carcinoma and cribriform DCIS (spherules are myoepithelial-derived).

entities.variants: Intraductal; periductal
entities.remarks: Benign myoepithelial proliferation; distinguish from adenomyoepithelioma and myoepithelial carcinoma.

entities.variants: Lactating breast; focal pseudolactational hyperplasia (non-pregnant, drug-related e.g. phenothiazines); with cystic hypersecretory features
entities.remarks: Hobnail vacuolated cells with secretions in lobules; benign; may mimic clear cell / secretory lesions.
Milk-retention cyst in lactation/post-lactation; may inspissate, rupture with lipogranulomatous reaction.

entities.variants: Plasma cell mastitis (inflammatory end of spectrum); obliterative mastitis
entities.remarks: Dilated subareolar ducts with inspissated secretions, foamy histiocytes (ochrocytes), periductal fibrosis ± calcification; perimenopausal; nipple discharge/retraction.

entities.variants: Post-traumatic; post-surgical/biopsy; post-radiation; post-reduction mammoplasty/flap; membranous (lipomembranous) fat necrosis; oil cyst
entities.remarks: Anucleate fat cells, lipid-laden histiocytes, giant cells, fibrosis and calcification; clinical/radiological mimic of carcinoma.

entities.variants: Haematoma; biopsy-cavity granulation tissue; epithelial displacement (into stroma/lymphovascular spaces/nodes); reparative changes; seroma
entities.remarks: Displaced epithelium after needle procedures can mimic invasion; look for haemorrhage, haemosiderin, granulation tissue along needle tract.

entities.variants: Lobular atrophy with epithelial atypia; stromal fibrosis; vascular changes (atypical stromal fibroblasts, vascular sclerosis)
entities.remarks: Atypical, enlarged, hyperchromatic TDLU epithelial cells in atrophic lobules — avoid misdiagnosis as recurrent carcinoma; see also atypical vascular lesion / post-RT angiosarcoma.

entities.variants: Tumour bed with fibrosis, elastosis, histiocytes, haemosiderin; residual cancer burden (RCB) assessment
entities.remarks: Document pCR vs residual disease (RCB class 0–III); treatment-related lobular/epithelial atypia.
Superficial thrombophlebitis of thoracoepigastric/lateral thoracic vein; cord-like subcutaneous induration; may be associated with trauma, surgery or underlying carcinoma.

entities.variants: Infarcted fibroadenoma; infarcted papilloma; infarction in pregnancy/lactation; anticoagulant (warfarin) necrosis
entities.remarks: Coagulative necrosis may mimic malignancy clinically; preserved ghost architecture.

entities.variants: Diffuse/incidental; nodular (tumoural PASH); fascicular PASH
entities.remarks: WHO 5th lists under fibroblastic/myofibroblastic tumours (tumour-like); complex anastomosing slit-like spaces lined by myofibroblasts (CD34+, PR+, ERG/CD31−) — distinguish from low-grade angiosarcoma.
Dense stromal fibrosis with atrophic ducts/lobules forming a palpable/imaging mass; premenopausal women.

entities.entity: Stromal multinucleated giant cells / benign stromal atypia
entities.remarks: Incidental, benign, often in interlobular stroma or fibroepithelial lesions; no clinical significance.

entities.variants: Localised (AL with MALT lymphoma/plasma cell neoplasm); systemic AL/AA
entities.remarks: Congo red apple-green birefringence; exclude underlying MALT lymphoma or plasma cell neoplasm.

entities.variants: Calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite); calcium oxalate (weddellite) crystals; dystrophic calcification
entities.remarks: Correlate with mammographic microcalcifications in core biopsies; oxalate crystals best seen under polarised light.

entities.variants: Infundibular cyst; post-traumatic/post-biopsy inclusion cyst
entities.remarks: Keratin-filled squamous cyst in subcutis/skin of breast or after needle procedures; may rupture with keratin granulomas.

entities.variants: Florid (active); intermediate; fibrous (inactive); unilateral/bilateral; physiological (neonatal, pubertal, senile); drug-induced, hormonal, cirrhosis-associated; pseudoangiomatous stroma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th lists under tumours of the male breast; ducts with gynaecomastoid (micropapillary) hyperplasia and periductal oedematous cellular stroma; no lobules typically. Gynaecomastoid hyperplasia may occur in women.
Enlargement due to adipose tissue only (obesity) without ductal/stromal proliferation.

entities.variants: Lactiferous duct hyperplasia; nipple duct ectasia; nipple fissure/erosion
entities.remarks: Benign; correlate with nipple adenoma and Paget disease.

entities.variants: Reactive follicular hyperplasia; silicone lymphadenopathy; dermatopathic changes
entities.remarks: Upper outer quadrant; may harbour metastasis or lymphoma; may be sentinel node.

WHO 5th: columnar cell lesion with low-grade (monomorphic) cytological atypia without architectural complexity; part of low-grade breast neoplasia family (with ADH, LN, low-grade DCIS, tubular ca); ER+, CK5/6−.

entities.variants: ADH in TDLU; ADH within papilloma (atypical focus <3 mm); ADH in radial scar / fibroadenoma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th: monotonous cells with rigid bridges/cribriform/micropapillary architecture, qualitatively like low-grade DCIS but ≤2 mm or ≤2 membrane-bound spaces; RR ~4–5; excision usually recommended on core biopsy.

entities.variants: Pagetoid spread into ducts
entities.remarks: WHO 5th non-invasive lobular neoplasia; discohesive monomorphic cells filling <50% of acini of a lobule without distension; E-cadherin loss / p120 cytoplasmic; RR ~4–5.

entities.variants: Classic LCIS (type A and B cells); florid LCIS (marked distension, confluent, may have necrosis/calcification); pleomorphic LCIS (grade 3 nuclei, may be apocrine, often necrosis)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th non-invasive lobular neoplasia; classic LCIS = risk factor & non-obligate precursor (RR ~8–10); florid and pleomorphic LCIS behave more aggressively and are managed like DCIS (clear excision); CDH1 alteration, E-cadherin negative.

entities.variants: Nuclear grade: low, intermediate, high. Architecture: cribriform, micropapillary, solid, papillary, flat (clinging), comedo (central necrosis). Cytological variants: apocrine, signet-ring/mucinous, neuroendocrine, spindle cell, squamous, clear cell, cystic hypersecretory DCIS. DCIS involving sclerosing adenosis/papilloma/radial scar/fibroadenoma
entities.remarks: Non-invasive (pTis) clonal neoplastic proliferation confined to ductal-lobular system; non-obligate precursor of invasive carcinoma. Report grade, necrosis, size/extent, margins, ER (± HER2 in some settings); low-grade DCIS ≥2 mm; myoepithelial layer present.
WHO 5th: atypical monotonous proliferation within papilloma measuring ≥3 mm (<3 mm = papilloma with ADH); high-grade atypia = DCIS regardless of size.
WHO 5th: DCIS with true fibrovascular cores lacking myoepithelial cells within papillae, but myoepithelium retained at duct periphery; often multiple ducts, usually low/intermediate grade.

WHO 5th: solid nodules with delicate fibrovascular cores, often neuroendocrine differentiation (synaptophysin/chromogranin) and extracellular mucin; ER+; staged as in situ (pTis) when nodules are rounded even if myoepithelium is absent at periphery; invasive when jigsaw/geographic pattern (see Malignant).
Cystic hypersecretory lesion with nuclear atypia/micropapillary proliferation, short of cystic hypersecretory DCIS.

entities.variants: Classic MGA; atypical microglandular adenosis; MGA-associated carcinoma (see Malignant)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th adenosis entity; haphazard infiltrative small round glands with eosinophilic secretions, single epithelial layer lacking myoepithelium but with basement membrane (laminin/collagen IV); S100+, ER−/PR−/HER2−. Considered a non-obligate precursor of triple-negative carcinoma (incl. acinic cell carcinoma) — complete excision advised.

entities.variants: Central (large duct, solitary) papilloma; peripheral (multiple) papillomas / papillomatosis; sclerosing papilloma; infarcted papilloma; papilloma with UDH, apocrine/squamous metaplasia, collagenous spherulosis; papilloma with ADH (atypical focus <3 mm)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th papillary neoplasm; arborising fibrovascular cores lined by epithelium and myoepithelium (p63, CK5/6 mosaic). Central: nipple discharge; peripheral: higher association with atypia/carcinoma. Papilloma with ADH carries increased risk (also see Preneoplastic for papilloma with DCIS).
WHO 5th adenoma; well-circumscribed, closely packed uniform tubules with two-cell layer and scant stroma; young women; may merge with fibroadenoma.

entities.variants: Lactational nodule (lactational change in tubular adenoma/fibroadenoma)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th adenoma; pregnancy/lactation; lobulated, secretory hobnail cells; may infarct.

WHO 5th adenoma; well-circumscribed glandular proliferation within a duct with sclerotic wall, often apocrine metaplasia; regarded by some as sclerosed papilloma; must not be mistaken for invasive carcinoma (myoepithelium retained).

WHO 5th epithelial-myoepithelial tumour; rare in breast (often subareolar, near papilloma); epithelial/myoepithelial cells with chondromyxoid stroma; PLAG1/HMGA2 rearrangements; mimic of metaplastic carcinoma.

entities.variants: Spindle cell; tubular; lobulated; mixed patterns; ER-positive and ER-negative types; with atypia
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; biphasic proliferation of luminal epithelial and abluminal myoepithelial cells (p63, calponin, SMMHC, CK5/6); ER-negative AMEs frequently HRAS Q61 hotspot ± PIK3CA/PIK3R1 mutations and higher risk of malignant transformation; may recur locally.

entities.variants: Usual (intracanalicular, pericanalicular patterns); cellular fibroadenoma; complex fibroadenoma (cysts >3 mm, sclerosing adenosis, epithelial calcifications, papillary apocrine change); juvenile fibroadenoma (cellular stroma, pericanalicular, gynaecomastoid epithelium; adolescents; may be giant); myxoid fibroadenoma (Carney complex association); fibroadenoma with infarction; fibroadenomatosis/fibroadenomatoid change; fibroadenoma with LCIS/DCIS/invasive carcinoma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th fibroepithelial tumour; commonest benign tumour of young women; MED12 exon 2 mutations frequent; cellular fibroadenoma vs benign phyllodes is the main differential (leaf-like architecture, periductal stromal condensation favour phyllodes).

WHO 5th; leaf-like architecture with periductal stromal hypercellularity; well-defined border, mild stromal cellularity/atypia, mitoses <2.5/mm² (<5/10 HPF), no stromal overgrowth; may recur locally; MED12, TERT promoter mutations.

entities.variants: Adenolipoma; myoid hamartoma (smooth muscle); chondrolipoma / chondroid hamartoma; hamartoma with PASH
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; well-circumscribed mass of disorganised normal breast components ('breast within a breast'); Cowden syndrome association when multiple.

entities.variants: Sclerosing papillomatosis pattern; papillomatosis pattern; adenosis pattern; mixed patterns (synonyms: florid papillomatosis of nipple, erosive adenomatosis)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; benign proliferation of collecting ducts of nipple with retained myoepithelium; serous/bloody discharge, erosion mimicking Paget disease; may coexist with carcinoma rarely.

WHO 5th (formerly syringomatous adenoma); infiltrative small comma/tadpole-shaped squamoid tubules and nests in nipple stroma, ER/PR−, p63+ outer cells; locally aggressive/recurs, does not metastasise — differential: low-grade adenosquamous carcinoma, tubular carcinoma.

entities.variants: Perilobular haemangioma (microscopic, incidental); cavernous; capillary; venous; complex; anastomosing haemangioma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th vascular tumour; well-circumscribed, no endothelial atypia, no dissection of lobules — key differential from well-differentiated angiosarcoma.
WHO 5th; diffuse proliferation of well-formed vascular channels involving large area of breast, surrounding but not invading lobules; rare; may recur.

entities.entity: Lymphangioma / lymphatic malformation and other benign vascular lesions
entities.variants: Lymphangioma (cystic hygroma); pyogenic granuloma (lobular capillary haemangioma) of nipple/breast skin; venous malformation
entities.remarks: Rare in breast parenchyma; mainly skin/subcutis of breast.
WHO 5th; self-limited clonal myofibroblastic proliferation (USP6 rearrangement, MYH9::USP6); tissue-culture-like spindle cells, extravasated RBCs, myxoid stroma; rapid growth.

entities.variants: Classic; collagenised/fibrous; epithelioid; cellular; infiltrative; lipomatous; myxoid; deciduoid; palisaded/schwannian-like; with atypia (atypical/pleomorphic)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; men and older women; bland spindle cells in short fascicles with thick hyalinised collagen bands; CD34+, desmin+, ER/PR/AR+; RB1 (13q14) loss — same family as spindle cell lipoma and cellular angiofibroma.
WHO 5th; S100+, SOX10+, CD68+ (granular cytoplasm, lysosomes), inhibin+; infiltrative and hard; important clinical/radiological mimic of carcinoma; rarely malignant.

entities.variants: Conventional; cellular; plexiform; ancient
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; Antoni A/B, Verocay bodies; S100/SOX10 diffuse.

entities.variants: Localised; diffuse; plexiform (NF1)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; NF1 association; NF1 patients have increased breast cancer risk.

entities.variants: Nipple-areolar (dartoic) leiomyoma; parenchymal leiomyoma; angioleiomyoma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; most arise in nipple-areolar complex; SMA/desmin/h-caldesmon+.

entities.variants: Conventional lipoma; spindle cell/pleomorphic lipoma (RB1 loss); chondroid lipoma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; distinguish from hamartoma (adenolipoma) and fat necrosis.

entities.variants: Conventional; cellular angiolipoma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; vascular component with fibrin thrombi; cellular angiolipoma mimics angiosarcoma (well-circumscribed, capsule, thrombi favour angiolipoma).

entities.entity: Other benign soft-tissue tumours of breast (rare)
entities.variants: Benign fibrous histiocytoma (dermatofibroma) of breast skin; glomus tumour; soft-tissue chondroma; benign fibrous lesions of skin
entities.remarks: Rare; classify per WHO Soft Tissue & Bone Tumours (5th ed).

entities.entity: Benign adnexal tumours of breast/nipple skin
entities.variants: Hidradenoma; syringoma; eccrine spiradenoma; pilomatricoma; seborrhoeic keratosis; hidradenoma papilliferum (ectopic)
entities.remarks: Arise from skin of breast; classify per WHO Skin Tumours; hidradenoma of breast may mimic carcinoma (CRTC1::MAML2).
WHO 5th; invasive focus/foci each ≤1 mm (pT1mi) usually associated with high-grade DCIS; multiple foci not summed; confirm absence of myoepithelium (p63/SMMHC).

entities.entity: Invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (IBC-NST)
entities.variants: Special morphological patterns (WHO 5th): medullary pattern (formerly medullary/atypical medullary carcinoma — now IBC-NST with medullary pattern, TIL-rich, often BRCA1/TNBC); oncocytic carcinoma; lipid-rich carcinoma; glycogen-rich clear cell carcinoma; sebaceous carcinoma; carcinoma with osteoclast-like stromal giant cells; pleomorphic carcinoma; carcinoma with choriocarcinomatous features; carcinoma with melanocytic features; carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation (<90% NE). Mixed types: IBC-NST with special-type component (10–90% special type); mixed ductal-lobular
entities.remarks: WHO 5th: commonest type (~70–75%); diagnosed when no special-type pattern or special type <10%; pure special type requires ≥90% of the pattern; 10–90% special type = mixed carcinoma. Nottingham (Elston-Ellis) grade 1–3; report ER, PR, HER2 (incl. HER2-low), Ki-67; TILs recommended in TNBC/HER2+. Molecular intrinsic subtypes: luminal A, luminal B, HER2-enriched, basal-like.

entities.variants: Classic; solid; alveolar; pleomorphic (grade 3 nuclei, may have apocrine/histiocytoid features); tubulolobular; signet-ring cell (histiocytoid) pattern; mixed lobular (non-classic combinations)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; ~10–15%; discohesive cells in single files/targetoid pattern; E-cadherin loss (CDH1 inactivation) with cytoplasmic p120; ER+ mostly (pleomorphic may be HER2+/AR+); multifocal/bilateral; unusual metastatic sites (peritoneum, GI tract, ovary, meninges, bone marrow).

WHO 5th; >90% open angulated tubules with single layer of low-grade cells, apical snouts, desmoplastic/elastotic stroma; ER+/PR+, HER2−; excellent prognosis; often with FEA/ADH/low-grade DCIS/LN (low-grade family).

entities.variants: Pure (>90%); mixed with tubular carcinoma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; invasive cribriform islands of low-grade cells; ER+; excellent prognosis; differential: cribriform DCIS, adenoid cystic carcinoma, collagenous spherulosis.

entities.variants: Type A (paucicellular, classic); type B (hypercellular, often neuroendocrine differentiation); mixed (with NST)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; >90% clusters of tumour cells floating in extracellular mucin pools; ER+/HER2−; favourable prognosis; older women.

WHO 5th; rare; cysts lined by tall columnar cells with abundant intracytoplasmic mucin, resembling ovarian/pancreatic counterpart; usually ER/PR/HER2 negative but favourable outcome; exclude metastasis.

entities.variants: Pure (>90%); mixed with NST
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; hollow/morula-like clusters in clear stromal spaces with 'inside-out' (reverse) polarity (EMA/MUC1 on stromal surface); high propensity for LVI and nodal metastasis; micropapillary pattern in mucinous carcinoma is a variant of mucinous.

entities.variants: Apocrine carcinoma (ER−/PR−/AR+ molecular apocrine); apocrine features in ER+ carcinoma; histiocytoid apocrine
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; >90% apocrine cells (abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli); AR+, GCDFP-15+; often HER2+ or triple-negative 'molecular apocrine' subtype.

entities.variants: Low-grade adenosquamous carcinoma; fibromatosis-like metaplastic carcinoma; spindle cell carcinoma; squamous cell carcinoma (incl. acantholytic, cystic); metaplastic carcinoma with heterologous mesenchymal differentiation (chondroid, osseous, rhabdomyoid, other); mixed metaplastic carcinoma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; mostly triple-negative (basal-like/claudin-low), poor chemosensitivity except low-grade forms. Spindle-cell lesions of breast: keratins (HMW CK, AE1/AE3, CK5/6, 34βE12) and p63 positivity favour metaplastic carcinoma over sarcoma/phyllodes. Low-grade adenosquamous and fibromatosis-like types behave indolently (local recurrence).
Clinical diagnosis (erythema/oedema/peau d'orange ≥1/3 of breast, cT4d); dermal lymphatic tumour emboli commonly but not required; any histological type, often high-grade NST; poor prognosis.
Usually triple-negative carcinoma (NST, acinic cell, matrix-producing metaplastic) arising in MGA; shares TP53 alterations with associated MGA.

entities.variants: Without invasion; with invasion (invasive component beyond capsule, usually NST)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; cystic papillary lesion with fibrous capsule, myoepithelium absent within papillae and usually at periphery; low/intermediate grade, ER+; staged as pTis when no invasion beyond capsule (stage invasive component only); excellent prognosis.
WHO 5th; invasive SPC — irregular, jigsaw/geographic nests infiltrating stroma; stage on invasive component; neuroendocrine & mucinous differentiation common.
WHO 5th; extremely rare; invasive carcinoma with >90% papillary architecture (fibrovascular cores) in the invasive component; exclude metastasis (lung, ovary, thyroid) and EPC/SPC.

WHO 5th rare/salivary gland-type; serous acinar differentiation with zymogen-like granules (lysozyme, α1-antichymotrypsin, EMA, S100); triple-negative; frequently associated with MGA; genomically TNBC-like (TP53).

entities.variants: Classic; solid-basaloid; adenoid cystic carcinoma with high-grade transformation
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; dual luminal (CK7, CD117) and myoepithelial/basaloid (p63, SMA, CK5/6) cells; true lumina and pseudolumina with basement membrane material; MYB::NFIB fusion t(6;9) or MYBL1 rearrangement; triple-negative but classic type has favourable prognosis.

WHO 5th; microcystic, solid and tubular architecture with eosinophilic/bubbly secretions; S100+, mammaglobin+, SOX10+; ETV6::NTRK3 fusion t(12;15) (pan-TRK IHC+); any age including children; indolent; NTRK inhibitors.

entities.variants: Low-grade; intermediate; high-grade
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; mucinous, intermediate and epidermoid cells; CRTC1::MAML2 fusion in subset (esp. low grade); typically triple-negative.
WHO 5th; extremely rare in breast; cytologically uniform cells in variable architecture (solid, cribriform, single files, targetoid); resembles salivary counterpart.

entities.entity: Tall cell carcinoma with reversed polarity
entities.remarks: WHO 5th (formerly solid papillary carcinoma with reverse polarity / breast tumour resembling tall cell variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma); solid papillary nests of columnar cells with apical nuclei, nuclear grooves/inclusions; IDH2 R172 hotspot ± TET2; mostly ER−; TTF1/thyroglobulin negative; indolent.

entities.variants: Malignant transformation of epithelial, myoepithelial or both components (includes myoepithelial carcinoma / carcinoma arising in AME)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; carcinoma arising in AME; often ER-negative, HRAS Q61 mutations; may metastasise haematogenously (lung, bone).
WHO 5th; biphasic malignant tumour with inner luminal ductal cells and outer clear myoepithelial cells; resembles salivary EMC; HRAS mutations reported.

entities.variants: NET grade 1; NET grade 2 (Nottingham grading)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; invasive tumour with ≥90% well-differentiated neuroendocrine morphology and uniform strong synaptophysin/chromogranin/INSM1 expression; ER+ usually; exclude metastatic NET (lung, GI). Distinct from IBC-NST with NE differentiation and mucinous type B/SPC with NE features.

entities.variants: Small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma; large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; poorly differentiated, high-grade NE carcinoma; often ER−; exclude metastasis from lung; may have associated DCIS/NST component supporting breast primary.

entities.variants: With underlying DCIS; with underlying invasive carcinoma; without detectable underlying carcinoma (rare); anaplastic/pigmented variants (melanin-laden, mimic melanoma)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; intraepidermal large clear-cytoplasm adenocarcinoma cells in nipple epidermis; CK7+, HER2+ (often), GATA3+, CAM5.2+, ER variable; S100/SOX10/HMB45− and p63− (vs melanoma, Bowen/SCC in situ, Toker cells — Toker cells CK7+ but bland, HER2−).

entities.variants: With heterologous malignant elements (osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, pleomorphic liposarcoma); with stromal overgrowth
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; all: marked stromal cellularity & atypia, ≥5 mitoses/mm² (≥10/10 HPF), stromal overgrowth, permeative border — OR presence of malignant heterologous elements (note: well-differentiated liposarcoma/ALT component alone is no longer sufficient for malignant designation); haematogenous metastasis (lung, bone) in up to ~25%; TERT promoter, TP53, EGFR, NF1 alterations.

entities.variants: Cutaneous ± parenchymal; well, moderately, poorly differentiated
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; arises in skin/breast after radiotherapy for breast cancer (median ~5–7 years); high-level MYC amplification (MYC IHC diffuse nuclear) — distinguishes from atypical vascular lesion; poor prognosis.

entities.variants: Low-grade (well-differentiated); intermediate; high-grade (poorly differentiated, solid/epithelioid, blood lakes, necrosis)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; young women (3rd–4th decade), parenchymal; anastomosing vascular channels dissecting lobules/fat, endothelial atypia; CD31/ERG/CD34+; MYC usually not amplified; grade correlates poorly with outcome in recent series.
WHO 5th; very rare; nipple-areolar or parenchymal; fascicles of atypical smooth muscle cells, mitoses, necrosis; exclude metaplastic carcinoma and malignant phyllodes with leiomyosarcomatous element.

entities.variants: Atypical lipomatous tumour/well-differentiated liposarcoma (see Neoplastic-Others); myxoid liposarcoma; pleomorphic liposarcoma; dedifferentiated liposarcoma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; primary breast liposarcoma rare — most liposarcomatous components arise in phyllodes tumour; myxoid liposarcoma in breast often actually phyllodes-associated (lacks DDIT3 rearrangement).

entities.variants: Primary extraskeletal osteosarcoma; chondrosarcoma; rhabdomyosarcoma (primary, adolescents); undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma; malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour; fibrosarcoma; synovial sarcoma; malignant granular cell tumour; Kaposi sarcoma (breast skin)
entities.remarks: Diagnosis of primary sarcoma requires exclusion of metaplastic carcinoma (extensive keratin/p63 panel) and malignant phyllodes (thorough sampling for epithelial component); classify per WHO Soft Tissue & Bone 5th ed.

entities.entity: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma)
entities.variants: With plasmacytic differentiation; with amyloid
entities.remarks: WHO 5th breast; one of the commonest primary breast lymphomas; lymphoepithelial lesions; CD20+, CD5−, CD10−; indolent.

entities.variants: Grade 1–2; grade 3A (classic FL)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th breast; CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2+ (t(14;18) in most).

entities.variants: Germinal centre B-cell (GCB) type; activated B-cell (non-GCB/ABC) type; high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC/BCL2 rearrangement (exclude)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th breast; commonest primary breast lymphoma; mostly ABC type (MYD88/CD79B); risk of CNS relapse; mimic of lobular/medullary-pattern carcinoma — keratin vs CD45/CD20.

entities.variants: Endemic; sporadic; immunodeficiency-associated; pregnancy/lactation-associated bilateral massive involvement
entities.remarks: WHO 5th breast; starry-sky pattern, Ki-67 ~100%, MYC rearrangement; often bilateral in young women during pregnancy/lactation.

entities.entity: Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL)
entities.variants: In-situ (effusion/seroma-confined, capsule-lining) type; infiltrative (mass-forming) type
entities.remarks: WHO 5th breast; T-cell lymphoma associated with textured implants; delayed seroma (~8–10 years post-implant); large pleomorphic CD30+ (strong uniform), ALK− cells in effusion/capsule; JAK/STAT3 activation; complete en bloc capsulectomy curative for confined disease. Send effusion fluid for cytology & CD30 IHC/flow.

entities.variants: Extramedullary plasmacytoma; myeloid sarcoma (granulocytic sarcoma); lymphoblastic lymphoma; classic Hodgkin lymphoma (rare, usually secondary); peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS; secondary involvement by systemic lymphoma/CLL/leukaemia
entities.remarks: Rare; classify per WHO Haematolymphoid Tumours 5th ed; myeloid sarcoma: MPO/CD117/CD34/lysozyme.

entities.entity: Carcinoma of the male breast (in situ and invasive)
entities.variants: DCIS (usually papillary/cribriform, low–intermediate grade); invasive carcinoma (mostly IBC-NST, also papillary/encapsulated papillary, lobular rare)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th tumours of the male breast; <1% of breast cancers; mostly ER+/PR+/AR+, luminal; BRCA2 germline association (also CHEK2, PALB2), Klinefelter syndrome, estrogen excess; nipple involvement and Paget disease common due to small breast volume.

entities.entity: Malignant cutaneous tumours of breast skin
entities.variants: Basal cell carcinoma (nipple-areola); squamous cell carcinoma of skin; melanoma of breast skin; extramammary-type adnexal carcinomas; Merkel cell carcinoma
entities.remarks: Primary skin malignancies; classify per WHO Skin Tumours; BCC of nipple may mimic Paget disease.

WHO 5th; intermediate features: well-defined to focally permeative border, moderate stromal cellularity/atypia, 2.5 to <5 mitoses/mm² (5–9/10 HPF), focal or absent stromal overgrowth; may recur, rarely metastasise. Not all criteria need to be present.
Regarded as a variant/form of phyllodes tumour (WHO 5th): non-circumscribed stromal proliferation around open tubules lacking leaf-like pattern; grade as phyllodes.

entities.variants: Lymphatic type; vascular (blood-vessel) type
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; post-radiation cutaneous vascular proliferation (circumscribed, superficial dermis, no multilayering/significant atypia); MYC not amplified; small risk of progression to angiosarcoma — complete excision & follow-up.

entities.variants: Sporadic; post-surgical/post-implant; FAP (Gardner) associated
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; locally aggressive, non-metastasising; infiltrative long sweeping fascicles of bland myofibroblasts entrapping ducts/lobules; nuclear β-catenin (CTNNB1 or APC mutation); keratin negative (vs fibromatosis-like metaplastic carcinoma).
WHO 5th; intermediate (rarely metastasising); myofibroblasts with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate; ALK rearrangement (ALK IHC+) in ~50%, also ROS1/NTRK fusions.

entities.entity: Other intermediate soft-tissue tumours in breast
entities.variants: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (breast skin; COL1A1::PDGFB, CD34+); solitary fibrous tumour (NAB2::STAT6, STAT6 nuclear); atypical lipomatous tumour / well-differentiated liposarcoma (MDM2 amplification); giant cell tumour of soft tissue
entities.remarks: Rare in breast; classify per WHO Soft Tissue & Bone Tumours 5th ed; ALT component in phyllodes does not by itself upgrade to malignant phyllodes.

entities.entity: Metastases to the breast (and secondary tumours)
entities.variants: Contralateral breast carcinoma; melanoma (commonest extramammary source in many series); lung carcinoma (adenocarcinoma, small cell); ovarian (high-grade serous) carcinoma; gastric/colorectal adenocarcinoma; renal cell carcinoma; neuroendocrine tumours (GI, lung); thyroid carcinoma; sarcomas; alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (adolescents); haematolymphoid (leukaemia/lymphoma) secondary involvement; mesothelioma (direct/metastatic)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th; ~0.5–2% of breast malignancies; clues: lack of in situ component, unusual morphology, multiple well-circumscribed nodules; IHC: GATA3, TRPS1, SOX10, mammaglobin, GCDFP-15 (breast) vs TTF-1/napsin A (lung), PAX8/WT1 (ovary), CDX2/SATB2 (GI), SOX10/S100/HMB45/Melan-A (melanoma). TRPS1 highly sensitive for breast including TNBC/metaplastic.

entities.variants: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (BRCA1 — TNBC/basal-like, medullary pattern; BRCA2 — luminal, male breast cancer); PALB2; Li-Fraumeni syndrome (TP53; HER2+ early-onset); Cowden / PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome (hamartomas, multiple papillomas); hereditary diffuse gastric cancer (CDH1 — lobular carcinoma); Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (STK11); ataxia-telangiectasia (ATM); CHEK2; NF1 (neurofibromatosis type 1); Lynch syndrome (mismatch-repair genes, minor); Carney complex (myxoid fibroadenomas, ductal adenoma)
entities.remarks: WHO 5th chapter on genetic tumour syndromes of the breast; listed for completeness (not single histological entities); germline testing per guidelines; BRCA-associated tumours eligible for PARP inhibitors.

entities.entity: Carcinoma of unknown primary presenting with axillary nodal metastasis (occult breast primary)
entities.remarks: Axillary nodal adenocarcinoma with occult breast primary (GATA3/TRPS1/ER/mammaglobin+); MRI breast; managed as stage II breast cancer.
